claim.claim-text: receiving, by a first aggregation server and from each of multiple client devices, impression data that includes, for each impression of a digital component recorded by the client device, (i) a first join key that is based on a first unique identifier for the client device or an application on the client device at which the impression occurred, (ii) encrypted impression data that has been encrypted using a first public key of the first aggregation server and using a second public key of a second aggregation server different from the first aggregation server, and (iii) encrypted impression time data that indicates a time at which the impression occurred; executing, by the first aggregation server in collaboration with a second aggregation server, secure multi-party computations using a secure multi-party computation protocol to generate chronological sequences of encrypted impression data and encrypted conversion data stored by the second aggregation server and to decrypt the encrypted impression data and the encrypted conversion data, including:

2. The computer-implemented method of claim 1, wherein the encrypted impression time data is encrypted using the first public key and the second public key and/or the encrypted conversion time data is encrypted using the first public key and the second public key.

3. The computer-implemented method of claim 1 or 2, wherein the second aggregation server is configured to receive, from each of at least a portion of the multiple client devices, conversion data that includes, for each conversion recorded by the client device, (i) one of the second join keys that is based on a second unique identifier for the client device or an application on the client device at which the conversion occurred and (ii) a second value comprising encrypted conversion data that has been encrypted using the first public key and the second public key, and (iii) encrypted conversion time data that indicates a time at which the conversion occurred.

4. The computer-implemented method of any preceding claim, wherein identifying, based on the first join keys and second join keys corresponding to conversions for which the multiple client devices provided conversion data to the second aggregation server, groups of encrypted conversion data and corresponding encrypted impression data comprising identifying encrypted conversion data for which the second join key matches a corresponding first join key for the corresponding impression data.

5. The computer-implemented method of any preceding claim, further comprising, for each chronological sequence of encrypted impression data and encrypted conversion data, attributing credit for a conversion in the encrypted conversion data to each impression of the encrypted impression data based at least in part on the chronological sequence of encrypted impression data and encrypted conversion data.

6. The computer-implemented method of any preceding claim, wherein executing the secure multi-party computations comprises, for each impression, encrypting, by the first aggregation server, the first join key and sending, by the first aggregation server and to the second aggregation server, a first tuple comprising the encrypted first join key, the encrypted impression data, and the encrypted impression time data.

7. The computer-implemented method of claim 6, wherein executing the secure multi-party computations comprises receiving, from the second aggregation server and for each conversion, a second tuple comprising an encrypted second join key generated by the second aggregation server by encrypting the second join key, the encrypted conversion data, and the encrypted conversion time data.
8. The computer-implemented method of claim 7, wherein executing the multi-party computations comprises:
9. The computer-implemented method of claim 8, wherein the second aggregation server is configured to:

one or more processors; and one or more storage devices storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to carry out the method of any preceding claim.
11. A computer readable storage medium carrying instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to carry out the method of any one of claims 1 to 9.
12. A computer program product comprising instructions which, when executed by one or more computers, cause the one or more computers to carry out the steps of the method of any of claims 1 to 9.
